text: Thursday morning, Geum marches into the Hunter Association's Busan branch with her ladle, Jaeha and Pim hurrying behind her.
She slams it on the branch chief's desk. The lid is at nine percent. Seventy-two hours. Good morning to you too, Okran.
And who is this? Pim, signal keeper. He heard it counting. Branch Chief Yang stares. Your husk heard it.
But Yang has known Geum for decades. If she says the sea is counting, he evacuates the harbour.
He reaches for the phone, and the screen on the wall lights up.
It's Deputy Director Hwang, calling from Seoul. I hear you have visitors.
Mr. Kang's reports have been found unreliable before, he says. Kanghan Marine is reinforcing the lid. There will be no evacuation.
Yang puts the phone down.
And as Hwang smooths his lapel, the underside flips up for an instant: a small silver hexagon.
Kanghan's pin. Still under his lapel.
Out the window, far out at sea, a black crane barge sits right over the lid. Enjoy your stay in Busan, Mr. Kang.
Pim winces at it. That boat never stops talking. It drills and talks and drills.
Outside, Yang apologises. Hwang signs his budget. Then I'll sign mine, Geum says. And Jaeha's phone buzzes.
It's Han Sora. A rooftop pool at eleven. Kanghan would like a word.
So Jaeha walks into a luxury hotel in a borrowed tracksuit, with a goblin.
Sora is waiting on a lounger in a black swimsuit, cocktail in hand. Mr. Kang. You dressed up.
Jaeha suddenly finds the sky very interesting. Nib is unimpressed.
The offer: consult for Kanghan Marine, bring his husks, save Busan. Name his price. His sister's art school. A house. A guild.
Her tablet shows the anchors Kanghan plans to use. Harpoons on huge chains, each link stamped with a mark.
Jaeha takes a chain link out of his pocket. The same mark.
These are the farm's chains. You don't want to hold the lid. You want to keep what's under it.
Keeping is a kind of saving, isn't it? The hospitals here run on cores too.
Jaeha stands up. Tell him no.
He said you'd say that, Sora says. He also said you'd come to us anyway.
On the way out, Nib steals the little umbrella from her drink.
Sora actually laughs.
That afternoon, a crowd gathers on the beach.
Lyra is trying the sea for the first time, on a live stream, in a swimsuit Bomi bought her.
Bomi has come down from Seoul with her drone. Trap Rats in Busan, day one. She bought the swimsuit, so she gets the views.
Four hundred thousand people are watching.
Jaeha studies a cloud. Pim points out that he's staring at a cloud. It's a very interesting cloud.
Meanwhile, tourists want selfies with the mascot. Pim is an adult signal officer.
Then a Kanghan PR team walks up to Lyra with a glossy folder. Kanghan Marine wants her as their face.
Billboards in every city. Applause every day. A very generous fee.
Applause and money: two of the three things Lyra asked for when she joined. Her fingers drift toward the pen.
She glances at Jaeha, and he doesn't stop her. It's your choice. It's a good fee.
Lyra hands the pen back with a smile. I already have a merchant. He's terrible at business. I'm keeping him.
Jaeha goes red to the ears.
On the stream, over a million people watch her turn down Kanghan.
Then a line of perfect white husks marches down the beach, carrying luggage.
Moon Ahin has arrived in a white summer dress, Saebyeok holding a parasol over her. She was passing.
Lyra informs her she's in the shot. Moon Ahin informs her that she is the shot.
But she's here for a reason. Her uncle is building a second farm, right here, and she has the board's order to inspect it.
So the heir of Kanghan takes a boat out to the barge.
Kanghan's engineers block the gangway. The Director's orders. Nobody boards. Not even the heir.
Her hand tightens on her baton. Saebyeok steps in front of her.
She turns away, white with anger. Tell my uncle I came.
Back on the beach, the two women share a lounger and refuse to speak to each other.
They wouldn't even tell her what they're doing. Then, Jaeha says, they'll ask someone who listens.
At five, they gather at the end of the breakwater, the barge far out on the golden sea.
Can Pim hear radio? He's a signal keeper. Radio is baby talk.
His wings open in field form, and his signal reaches out toward the barge.
Through the link, Jaeha hears it too. Kanghan drills the lid tomorrow at six.
To set their anchors before it breaks, Pim relays.
Then someone on the barge asks what happens if the lid goes while they're drilling. They chain it as it comes up. Director's orders.
Geum's steel arm twitches hard.
They'll crack a ten-year lid to put a leash on what's under it. Moon Ahin goes white. He'd do it to a whole city.
Jaeha writes it all down.
Pim's wings fold round him. Boss. They're going to break it to keep it.
Out at sea, the barge's floodlights snap on, and the drills go down.
